title: Chapter 136: What Happened to Our Friendship?
html:
“Something’s wrong.” An oppressive sensation closed around Wang Wenlong, as though he were sinking through the deep ocean. Pressure built in his chest. He bent to collect the name tags without delay.

As his fingers brushed the well’s bottom, they found something thumb-sized protruding from beneath the sand.

“Another trap?” Rather than touch it directly, Wang Wenlong cautiously brushed away the surrounding sand.

“What’s buried here?” His fingers touched something softer and colder than sand. As the grains slipped away, a human face emerged. The protrusion had been the tip of its nose.

“F*ck!” Wang Wenlong snatched his hands back. He had carefully inspected the well before jumping. “That immoral bastard buried this under the sand!”

Had he known a “body” lay beneath him, he would never have entered alone. Panicking, he threw the tags out. “Pei Hu, pull me up! There’s a mannequin in the well!”

“A mannequin?” Pei Hu aimed the phone downward, and the face in the sand seemed to look back. He shuddered and extended one hand. “Strange. The well didn’t look this deep when you jumped.”

Wang Wenlong gripped Pei Hu’s arm and braced his feet against the claw-marked wall. Just as he began hauling himself up, something cold touched his ankle. His legs buckled, dropping him back into the well.

“Wenlong, what’s wrong?”

“Something touched me earlier.” Wang Wenlong looked at his ankle, but there was nothing there.

“Could it have been a lizard or tiny bug?”

“No idea.” Even without being touched, sand continued sliding away from the “body.” Soon half its torso was exposed, as if the mannequin were trying to sit up.

“It can move? This can’t be an actor. A real person would have cried out when I landed on them.” Wang Wenlong’s thoughts began to unravel. “Pei Hu, get me out!”

Outside the well, Pei Hu heard his voice and quickly reached down. “Grab onto my hand!”

For once, Pei Hu acted bravely. Holding the phone in one hand, he reached down with the other. His thick arm looked strangely reassuring.

“Okay!” Reassured by his companion’s voice, Wang Wenlong seized Pei Hu’s hand and climbed. He braced against the wall and tried to leap the final distance. Just before reaching the mouth, something clamped onto both his dangling legs.

“F*ck!” He was dragged down. Wang Wenlong looked behind him in disbelief and felt ice flood his veins. The face in the sand had opened its eyes.

“Did the mannequin pull me down?” Its eyes seemed to follow him through the well.

“This is too much.” Pressing himself against the wall, Wang Wenlong looked up. The circle of light seemed even farther away. “I can’t stay here. Pei Hu!”

“Keep your voice down! I think someone is coming.” Pei Hu reached both hands into the well. “Let’s try again.”

Pei Hu pulled with all his strength, but something again stopped Wang Wenlong.

Prepared this time, Wang Wenlong looked down as soon as pressure closed around his ankle. Nothing was visible there, but a female “body” had surfaced beneath the spot where he had been standing.

“Two mannequins? I was standing on her head?” Cold dread filled him. “How many are buried here? Whoever designed this place is insane. They buried mannequins and waited for visitors to jump on top of them.”

Clinging to Pei Hu, he kicked wildly, trying to dislodge whatever held him.

“Stop thrashing! I can’t hold you!” Red-faced with effort, Pei Hu braced one hand on the well and pulled again as his unease deepened.

Pei Hu kept scanning his surroundings. When he looked toward the corridor, his heart froze. A girl stood at the junction with her head bowed. Her blood-darkened uniform made her skin appear deathly pale.

“That’s the mannequin I dragged from the classroom!” The air entering his lungs felt cold, and his arms began shaking. “Didn’t her head fall off? An employee must have repaired her and left her there. A mannequin can’t move by itself.”

“Pull! Quick! The mannequins have opened their eyes!” Wang Wenlong yelled from inside the well. It sounded like the man was crying.

At the junction, the mannequin’s head rose with a creak. Her purple, blood-speckled face turned toward the well.

“There must be a mechanism in the neck. That explains the movement.” Pei Hu drew a deep breath and faced the well again. “Don’t get distracted. Save Wenlong first.”

He tried to focus, but his gaze strayed toward the corridor. The girl had left the junction and entered the left-hand passage.

She stood in its center, smiling at him. Pei Hu’s breath quickened, his palms sweated, and his whole body trembled.

“Why are you spacing out?” Something like seaweed coiled around Wang Wenlong’s calves. No matter how he kicked, he could not break free. Then both mannequins in the well opened their eyes. Nothing mattered except escaping. “Pull me up!”

Pei Hu hauled him several centimeters higher. A cold draft flowed from the corridor, carrying a faint creak. Pei Hu glanced sideways.

The mannequin had collapsed. Her smiling head rolled rapidly toward the well, propelled by an invisible hand.

The suffocated girl’s face drew closer. Terror distorted Pei Hu’s features. At last, he obeyed his instincts. Without hesitation, he released Wang Wenlong and sprinted into Room 303 with astonishing speed, slamming the door behind him.

Without support, Wang Wenlong slid back into the well. As safety vanished inches beyond his grasp, abject terror froze across his face.
